newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish GNP rises by 7.9 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkish GNP rises by 7.9 percent in 1996.

text.p: Turkish gross national product (GNP) rose by a real 7.9 percent in 1996, the second such increase in two years, the state institute of statistics said on Monday.
The institute said in a statement that fourth quarter 1996 GNP was up by 8.8 percent compared to the same period in 1995 and per capita income increased by 6.1 percent to $2,928.
The increase in gross domestic product in 1996 was a real 7.2 percent, according to the statement.
The figures did not affect the financial markets, which were predicting a rise of between 7.5 and eight percent for GNP, brokers said.
GNP had risen by eight percent in 1995 and also by eight percent in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Turkey often enjoys high growth, but this is coupled with high inflation, currently around 78 percent annually, and a yawning budget deficit, which was at 8.2 percent of GNP in 1996.
